title: Homemade Caramel Popcorn
excerpt: There is something wonderfully old-fashioned about a bowl of caramel popcorn cooling on the kitchen counter, its buttery sweetness filling the house with memories of movie nights and school parties. This golden, crisp treat is just right for Halloween gatherings, cozy films, and little hands eager to sneak a handful.

Why You'll Love This Caramel Popcorn

  • It has that classic buttery, brown sugar flavor everyone remembers.
  • The oven helps create crisp, golden clusters with a lovely crunch.
  • It is a wonderful treat for movie nights, school parties, and Halloween gatherings.
  • The recipe makes enough to share, with a few clusters left for sneaking from the bowl.
  • Simple pantry ingredients turn into a special homemade snack.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients before you begin, and you will be on your way to a big bowl of golden homemade goodness.

  • Popcorn kernels - 1 cup
  • Vegetable oil - 2 tablespoons
  • Unsalted butter - 1/2 cup
  • Light brown sugar - 1 cup packed
  • Light corn syrup - 1/4 cup
  • Fine salt - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Baking soda - 1/2 teaspoon

How to Make Caramel Popcorn

Plan for 15 minutes of preparation and 55 minutes of cooking, including the oven time. Let the popcorn cool completely before breaking it into clusters, so the caramel can set into a crisp coating.

Step 1: Preheat the Oven

Preheat your oven to 250°F. The low temperature will help dry and crisp the caramel coating without scorching it.

Step 2: Prepare the Baking Sheets

Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper. Set them nearby so the coated popcorn can be spread out easily later.

Step 3: Heat the Oil

Pour the vegetable oil into a large heavy-bottomed pot. Warm it over medium heat until the oil is ready for the kernels.

Step 4: Add the Kernels

Add the popcorn kernels to the pot and cover it with the lid. Keep the lid in place while the kernels begin to pop.

Step 5: Pop the Corn

Shake the covered pot gently from time to time to help the kernels pop evenly. Continue until there are several seconds between pops, then remove the pot from the heat.

Step 6: Transfer the Popcorn

Carefully transfer the popped popcorn to a large mixing bowl. Check for any unpopped kernels as you move it over, since they are best left out of the finished treat.

Step 7: Melt the Butter

Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Keep an eye on it and lower the heat if needed to prevent browning.

Step 8: Add the Caramel Ingredients

Stir the brown sugar, corn syrup, and salt into the melted butter. Mix until the ingredients are combined and the sugar begins to dissolve.

Step 9: Boil the Caramel

Bring the caramel mixture to a boil and cook it for 4 minutes without stirring. Stay close to the stove and use care, since the hot caramel can cause burns.

Step 10: Add the Baking Soda

Remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in the baking soda, which will make the caramel foam slightly and become easier to coat the popcorn.

Step 11: Coat the Popcorn

Pour the hot caramel over the popcorn. Toss carefully with a sturdy spoon or spatula until as much of the popcorn as possible is coated.

Step 12: Bake the Coated Popcorn

Bake the coated popcorn for 45 minutes at 250°F. Stir it every 15 minutes so the caramel continues to spread evenly over the popcorn.

Step 13: Spread on Baking Sheets

Spread the warm caramel popcorn onto the prepared baking sheets. Separate large clumps gently if needed, taking care with the hot coating.

Step 14: Cool Completely

Let the popcorn cool completely on the baking sheets. Once the caramel is firm, break the popcorn into bite-sized clusters.

Pro Tips for Making Caramel Popcorn

  • Use a large, heavy-bottomed pot for popping so the kernels heat evenly.
  • Keep the caramel mixture at a steady boil for the full 4 minutes for the best coating.
  • Work carefully when tossing the popcorn, since freshly made caramel is very hot.
  • Stir the popcorn every 15 minutes during baking to help prevent sticky patches.
  • Let the finished popcorn cool fully before storing it, or trapped warmth may soften the clusters.

How to Serve Caramel Popcorn

  • Fill small bowls or paper bags for a cozy movie night treat.
  • Set it out in a large serving bowl at a Halloween gathering or school party.
  • Package cooled clusters in clear bags with simple ribbons for a homemade gift.
  • Serve it alongside apple slices or fresh fruit for a sweet snack table.
  • Add a handful to lunch boxes once the popcorn is completely cool and securely packed.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cool the caramel popcorn completely before storing it.
  • Keep it in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.
  • If the clusters soften, spread them on a baking sheet briefly before serving.

Freezing

  • Freezing is not recommended because moisture can make the caramel coating lose its crisp texture.
  • For the best flavor and crunch, make only what you can enjoy within the storage period.

Reheating

  • To refresh softened popcorn, spread it in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
  • Warm it in a 250°F oven for 5 to 10 minutes, watching closely so the caramel does not scorch.
  • Let it cool completely before serving or returning it to an airtight container.

Final Thoughts

There is a little kitchen magic in turning a few humble ingredients into a crisp, golden bowl of caramel popcorn. Make a batch, share it generously, and enjoy every sweet, crunchy bite.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making and storing this old-fashioned favorite.

Why is my caramel popcorn sticky?

Sticky popcorn usually needs more time to dry and crisp. Bake it as directed, stir it regularly, and allow it to cool completely before storing.

Can I use salted butter?

Unsalted butter gives you better control over the flavor. If salted butter is all you have, reduce or omit the added fine salt.

How do I keep caramel popcorn crisp?

Cool it fully before placing it in an airtight container. Keep the container at room temperature and protect the popcorn from humidity.

Can I make this recipe ahead of time?

Yes, you can make it up to 1 week ahead. Store the cooled clusters in an airtight container and refresh them briefly in a low oven if needed.
